appliesTo: developers and deployers of automated employment-related decision technology; AI-companion operators; frontier developers; generative-AI providers; social-media platform operators

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 9(a) — 'shall ensure that it is disclosed to each such employee or applicant who interacts with such technology'; see also § 5(b) — 'provide a clear and conspicuous notice to a user disclosing that the user is communicating with an artificial intelligence companion'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: § 5(a)(1)(A)(i) — 'Uses evidence-based methods to (I) detect any user expression to the artificial intelligence companion clearly indicating a risk of suicide, self-harm or imminent physical violence'
dutySources.age-assurance: § 39(b)(1)(A)(i) — 'The covered operator has used commercially reasonable and technically feasible methods to determine that the covered user is not a covered minor'
dutySources.consent-workflow: § 39(b)(1)(A)(ii) — 'the covered operator has obtained verifiable consent from the covered minor's parent or legal guardian to recommend, select or prioritize media items'
dutySources.watermarking: § 15(b)(1)(A) — 'include provenance data in any audio, image or video content'
dutySources.takedown-process: § 2(c)(1) — 'establish and maintain a reasonable internal process through which (A) a covered employee of such large frontier developer may anonymously submit a report'
dutySources.registration-filing: § 26 — 'shall disclose to the department, in a form and manner prescribed by the Labor Commissioner, whether the layoffs'

sources.covers: §§ 8(a), 10 — 'shall provide to the deployer of such automated employment-related decision technology all information' (developer duty); 'a written notice disclosing: (1) That the deployer has deployed an automated employment' (deployer duty)
sources.trigger: § 7(5) — ''Employment-related decision' (A) means any decision, made based on any individual's personal data, to hire, promote, discipline or discharge such individual'
sources.consumerNotice: § 10 — 'shall, before such employment-related decision is made, provide to such employee or applicant a written notice'
sources.penaltyMax: § 2(e) — 'civil penalty in an amount that does not exceed one thousand dollars per violation'
sources.enforcer: § 12 — 'shall constitute an unfair or deceptive trade practice for the purposes of subsection (a) of section 42-110b of the general statutes and shall be enforced solely by the Attorney General' (same formula in §§ 1(c), 5(c), 6(c), 15(c))
sources.cureDays: § 12 — 'If such person fails to cure such violation within sixty days of receipt of such notice of violation, the Attorney General may bring an action'

flags: Omnibus act spanning multiple families; adm-governance coded from the employment-ADM core (§§ 7–14) — also contains frontier-safety provisions (§ 2: whistleblower protections, anonymous internal reporting, $1,000/violation penalty), chatbot-safeguards provisions (§§ 4–6: crisisProtocol required, aiDisclosure at first interaction per 24-hour period then hourly for minors/every 3 hours for adults, parentalTools 'tools to manage minor users' screen time and account settings', ageThreshold 18 'younger than eighteen years of age'), and provenance-transparency provisions (§ 15: watermark required for generative-AI systems with 'more than one million users per month')

trigger coded consequential-decisions is lossy: the ADM regime covers only employment-related decisions (hire, promote, discipline, discharge, renewal, training selection, terms of employment), not all consequential decisions
§ 1 imposes subscription key-terms disclosure on subscription-based AI providers — fits no listed duty

§§ 13–14 make ADM use a non-defense in employment-discrimination cases and let tribunals consider 'evidence of anti-bias testing or similar proactive efforts' — anti-bias testing is permissive evidence, not a required bias-audit

§ 39 regulates social-media covered platforms' algorithmic feeds for minors (age determination, parental consent, default one-hour limit, Surgeon General warning, annual public disclosure) — feed rules are not AI-specific; annual public disclosure (§ 39(e)) fits no listed duty

penaltyMax $1,000/violation applies only to § 2 (frontier-developer whistleblower) violations; all other regimes are CUTPA unfair trade practices enforced solely by the Attorney General with no penalty amount stated in this text and no private right of action
cureDays 60 is discretionary ('may... issue a notice of violation') and applies only to §§ 8–11 violations occurring on or before December 31, 2027

Bill also contains substantial non-company provisions coded here per the mixed-bill rule: public-sector duties (§§ 36–38: state-agency AI inventory, impact assessments, use/procurement restrictions), a regulatory-sandbox plan (§ 3), an independent-verification pilot program (§ 33), and workforce-development/education programs (Connecticut AI Academy §§ 17, 19–22, 30; education §§ 23, 27, 34; studies and working groups §§ 16, 18, 29, 31–32, 35)
